source_text:
2.12 Ἀκοῆς θήρα
Ἀνέγνων <τι> τοῖς μὲν πολλοῖς ἄπιστον, ἐμοὶ δὲ ἀμφιβαλλόμενον, διὰ δὲ τὸ
παράδοξον καὶ τοῦτο ἀνήγαγον· φασίν τινες Μαυρουσίους [ἔθνος δέ ἐστι τοῦτο]
ἐπερεισαμένους τὸν αὐχένα ξύλῳ, ἀκώλυτον εἰς ἀκοὴν ἐπαφεῖναι τὸ οὖς, ὀλίγον τε
ὑποσκάψαντας βόθρον καὶ κατακειμένους. Τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ δρᾶν καὶ τοὺς Γαλατῶν τῶν
ἑσπερίων ἀκούεται λῃστάς. Αὐτοσχέδιος αὕτη θήρα ἀκοῆς. Ὡς ἂν δέ τις ἐν μεγάλῳ
στρατοπέδῳ ἤτοι τὰ τῶν ἑαυτοῦ στρατιωτῶν βουλεύματα [καὶ] ἢ τὰ τῶν πολεμίων
βουλεύματα θελήσῃ μαθεῖν, φρέαρ ὀρύξας βαθύ, οἷον βούλεται καθιέτω,
ἐπικαλύψας τὸ στόμιον ἱματίῳ τῷ τυχόντι· οὐδὲ ἓν τὸν ἐγκαθήμενον λήσεται, ἀλλά
σοι τὰ εἰρημένα ἢ τὰ ἠχήσαντα ὡς μαντευόμενος διηγήσεται.
pass_a_gloss: 2.12 Hunting of hearing. I-read something to-the-many unbelievable, to-me but being-doubted, but through the paradoxical this too I-brought-up; they-say some Mauretanians [a-nation but is this] having-rested the neck on-a-wood, unhindered into hearing to-let-go the ear, and a-little having-dug-under a pit and lying-down. And the same to-do also the of-Gauls of-the-western is-heard brigands. Improvised this hunting of-hearing. As if someone in a-great camp either the of-his-own soldiers plans or the of-the-enemies plans should-wish to-learn, a-well having-dug deep, of-what-sort he-wishes let-him-let-down, having-covered the mouth with-a-cloak the-chance; not even one-thing the sitting-in will-escape, but to-you the things-said or the things-sounded as being-an-oracle he-will-narrate.
pass_b_english: A hunt of hearing. I read something unbelievable to the many, but for me in doubt, and because of the paradox I brought this up too. Some say that the Mauretanians — this is a nation — resting the neck on a piece of wood, let the ear go unhindered into hearing, having dug a little pit and lying down. And the brigands of the western Gauls are heard to do the same. This is an improvised hunt of hearing.

If someone in a great camp should wish to learn either the plans of his own soldiers or the plans of the enemy, having dug a deep well, let him let down whatever sort of man he wishes, having covered the mouth with whatever cloak is at hand: not one thing will escape the man sitting in, but he will narrate to you the things said or the things sounded, as if giving an oracle.

choices.english: resting the neck on a piece of wood
choices.why: The neck is propped on wood so the ear hangs free. Not a stake driven through the neck.
rejected: driven a wooden stake through their necks
leaning a wood into the neck

choices.why: Same people as 7.16. Not a personal name Maurosius.
rejected: Moors as a later ethnonym forced

choices.english: not one thing will escape the man sitting in
choices.why: λανθάνω with accusative of the person: nothing escapes his notice. The CF crib inverted it.
rejected: not one of those seated will escape
the sitter will not be caught

choices.english: let him let down whatever sort of man he wishes
choices.why: A person is lowered into the well. Not 'cover the well as he wishes'.
rejected: let the well be covered as he wishes

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
